chapter: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
title: Lu's brother August and the dime for new tunes
summary: Lu's brother, the fifth August in the family line, paid her a dime for each new tune she hummed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: His name was August DuPont. There was five Augusts in our family.

My father was named August. My brother was named August. He named his son August. And then his son is named August. So now we've got five. We've got August, Senior, August, Junior, August the Third, August the Fourth and August the Fifth.
When my brother was young, he got a job on the railroad, and he would be out six days and he'd come home

six days. So when he'd come home, he'd say to me, "What's the new tune?" So anything I could hum, he could play on the piano. So I'd hum anything, and he'd give me a dime! So when he'd go somewhere... Like, he had come back and he had moved in town. He'd come back out here in Pollard's Land to play the piano, and he said, "Nobody knows those tunes that you hum." "Oh," I said, "they live back of the tracks. They don't know those new tunes." I said, "That's a new tune. Give me my dime!" So he'd give me the dime. I'd give him sometimes the dime back to show me some Blues chords on the piano, you know. So that's how I... I'd always have a new tune for him after those six days....
So I could get that dime, yeah.
